newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels says Europe needs more flexible jobs.
newsitem.headline: Brussels says Europe needs more flexible jobs.

text.p: European companies need to find more flexible working practices without compromising the security of their workers, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

Introducing less rigid, hierarchical arrangements for pay and working time was necessary to create jobs and keep European Union firms competitive on the world stage, the EU's executive Commission said in a discussion paper.
It said traditional types of job were already being replaced by practices such as downsizing, outsourcing, subcontracting and teleworking -- working from home by computer.

But it said existing labour laws were unable to offer satisfactory cover for workers operating under these new conditions, where collective agreements are increasingly being replaced by individual job contracts.

"Individual workers...should not be penalised for adopting such working patterns. This means that the multitude of different forms of employment...must be supported by appropriate social protection systems," the Commission stressed.
EU Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn plans over the next six months to hold a series of discussions on future policy with EU governments, employers and trade unions.
"We are entirely in favour of flexibility," Olivier Richard of the European Employers' lobby UNICE told Reuters.

The European Trade Union Confederation said it also supported more modern forms of work, which would let people operate more freely and regularly update their skills to keep abreast of advances in technology.

But workers would have to be involved in company decisions to introduce these new forms of work and they would have to be covered by good social security regulations, the confederation's Wim Bergans said.
